name: Carousel
purpose: Present measured carousel pages with accessible navigation, multiple visible items, optional autoplay and native scroll motion.
useWhen: Peer content benefits from one or several visible slides with optional navigation, touch scrolling and mouse drag.

avoidWhen.condition: Every item must be visible at once for comparison.

composition: Compose Root, Viewport, Track and uniquely valued Slide parts. Add the controls appropriate to the content.
Use useCarousel and RootProvider for one externally accessible controller. Choose value-based or page-based control, not both.

rules.statement: When automatic rotation is enabled, include visible RotationControl, Previous, and Next controls; Picker controls remain optional.
Keep grouped PickerItem controls to a small set because each native picker button is a tab stop.
Keep styled viewport motion instant until Root exposes data-initialized, then enable the ordinary motion recipe so SSR hydration cannot start a competing native snap animation.
Do not place essential content only in a slide that users cannot reach without waiting for automatic rotation.
Derive automatic indicators and progress from pageSnapPoints, not raw item count. Several visible items can share one snap page.
Visible peer slides remain interactive; do not add application inert or aria-hidden rules based solely on the selected value.
Never clone authored slides. Short-content loops may settle instantly when smooth cyclic placement would require duplication.
Use value/defaultValue or page/defaultPage exclusively. Keep stable Slide values and supply index for server-known page visibility.
Custom viewport CSS disables scroll snapping during data-programmatic and data-dragging; slides apply the measured --atom-carousel-shift translation.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using Tabs for decorative dots, enabling autoplay without a stop control, reusing SwipeableItem, or adding custom timers and aria-hidden logic around Carousel.
commonMistakes.correction: Use Carousel's optional grouped Picker, complete autoplay controls, and Atom-owned state, pause, scrolling, and inactive-slide contract.

validation: Verify controlled and uncontrolled selection, Previous/Next boundaries, last-to-first forward motion, first-to-last backward motion, picker selection, native touch scrolling, LTR and RTL, and external value changes.

Verify autoplay timing, focus stop without automatic restart, temporary hover and document-visibility pause, visible rotation control, live-region mode, inactive inert state, labels, and reduced-motion handling in the styled layer.
